acquisition method: Acquisition was performed in data-dependent acquisition (DDA) mode
alkylation reagent: alkylated in the dark with 60 nmol iodoacetamide (25°C, 30 min)
alkylation concentration: alkylated in the dark with 60 nmol iodoacetamide (25°C, 30 min)... alkylated in the dark with 180 nmol iodoacetamide (30 min at 25°C)
cleavage agent: digestion with endoproteinase LysC (1:10 LysC weight: Cell lysate weight, overnight at 37°C; Wako, cat # 129-02541) and then diluted 2-fold with 200 mM ammonium bicarbonate for trypsin digestion (1:10 w:w, 8 h at 37°C; Promega, cat # V5113)
collision energy: Fragment ion spectra were produced via collision-induced dissociation (CID) at normalized collision energy of 35%
fragmentation method: Fragment ion spectra were produced via collision-induced dissociation (CID) at normalized collision energy of 35%
instrument: Samples were analyzed using a LTQ-Orbitrap Velos Pro-mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, San Jose, CA, USA)
ionization type: The mass spectrometer was operated in positive ionization mode with nano spray voltage set at 2.1 kV
labeling: we performed free-label mass spectrometry analyses of M. agalactiae and M. pneumoniae
mass analyzer: they were acquired in the ion trap mass analyzer
precursor tolerance: For peptide identification, a precursor ion mass tolerance of 7 ppm was used for the MS1 level
fragment tolerance: The fragment ion mass tolerance was set to 0.5 Da for MS2 spectra.
ptm: Oxidation of methionine (variable); N-terminal protein acetylation (variable); carbamidomethylation on cysteine (fixed)
Oxidation of methionine and N-terminal protein acetylation were used as variable modifications, with carbamidomethylation on cysteine set as a fixed modification.
reduction reagent: 10 μg of lysate samples were reduced with 30 nmol dithiothreitol (37°C, 60 min)
reduction concentration: reduced with 30 nmol dithiothreitol (37°C, 60 min)... reduced with 90 nmol dithiothreitol (30 min at 56°C)
